title: Government memo warning about an iPhone update
summary: An image shared online claimed to be a Homeland Security Investigations memo saying an iOS 27 update secretly listens to nearby conversations and sends them to Apple for ads. Lead Stories found the memo was not real, and several AI detectors flagged the image as AI-made.
tell: A scary official-looking memo that only shows up as a screenshot, with no agency or Apple announcement behind it, deserves doubt.

title: Rockstar letter delaying GTA VI to 2027
summary: An Instagram post shared what looked like a Rockstar Games letter saying Grand Theft Auto VI was pushed back a full year to November 2027. Lead Stories found no such announcement from Rockstar or any major news outlet, and the post itself was tagged as ragebait.
tell: A delay this big would be on the company's own news page and everywhere in the news, not just one social post.

title: Sabrina Carpenter and co-stars in a Palantir ad
summary: A post claimed a photo of Sabrina Carpenter, Margaret Qualley and Madelyn Cline was an ad for the tech company Palantir. Lead Stories found it was a behind-the-scenes still from a Carpenter music video, edited to add Palantir branding, and posted by an account that calls itself satire.
tell: Check the posting account's bio: this one says all its posts are satire.

title: A nationwide 90-day blackout starting Nov. 17
summary: TikTok posts, one using an edited clip of the president, claimed a 90-day nationwide blackout would start Nov. 17. PolitiFact rated it false: the clip was doctored, and what is actually planned that day is a national Emergency Alert System test on TV and radio.
tell: No agency announced a blackout, and urgent warnings with no named official source are a red flag.

title: King Charles's "urgent address" about his son
summary: A website story claimed King Charles III gave a tearful emergency address about a tragedy involving his son, with a photo of him crying. Lead Stories found no such speech on the royal family's site or in the news, and detection tools flagged the photo as AI-made.
tell: Read past the headline: the story's own text admits there's no verified evidence the address happened.

title: Travelers sleeping in a U.S. airport during the ground stop
summary: A viral clip was shared as showing crowds sleeping in an American airport during the nationwide FAA ground stop on Nov. 13. Lead Stories found the video was most likely made with AI and is not real footage.
tell: Look for odd details: piles of bedroom pillows, two identical women in matching pink hoodies, bodies blending together, and soda-brand posters announcing cancellations.

title: Jensen Huang quote about "focusing on women"
summary: A meme quoted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang saying smart people don't waste time focusing on women. Lead Stories found no evidence he ever said it and no news coverage of the remark.
tell: The quote names no source, date or event, and no news outlet reported it.

title: Saluting veteran at a Veterans Day parade
summary: A video of a scarred veteran being saluted at a parade was shared as real. Lead Stories found it was made with AI.
tell: Drumsticks vanish, medals melt into the uniform and the flag's stripes change width.

title: Colosseum and Eiffel Tower lit blue for the midterms
summary: Photos claimed the Colosseum and Eiffel Tower were lit blue for Democratic midterm wins. Lead Stories found they were made with AI.
tell: Neither landmark's own website or social media showed any such lighting.

title: Pennsylvania voter registration "scheme" video
summary: A post said a video proved 2026 voter registration fraud in Pennsylvania. Lead Stories found it was a 2024 press conference about the previous election.
tell: Check when a video was first posted. Old clips with new captions are a common trick.

title: Sharp photo of the Florida jet crash
summary: A crisp photo of the Florida jet crash seemed to show a missing wing. Lead Stories found it was apparently dashcam video "cleaned up" with AI.
tell: It looked sharper than any real footage, and the real video shows both wings.

title: Florida jet crash video is real, not AI
summary: A post claimed dashcam video of the Florida jet crash was "100%" AI. PolitiFact found it was real and confirmed by major news outlets.
tell: Calling something "AI" can be false too. Check whether trusted news outlets confirmed it.
